chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Sa'dan bin Muslim, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'A man has a concubine of his, and she has given birth to him, and her child has died, then he emancipates her.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not permissible for her to marry until her waiting period of three months has elapsed.'
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for an emancipated concubine after her child dies?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the specific 'iddah of emancipation (iddat al-tasreeh) for a concubine who has borne a child to her master, mandating a three-month period after her release from bondage. This ruling distinguishes her status from that of a free wife, reflecting the juristic consensus that her waiting period is determined by the time of her emancipation rather than the death of the child or the master, ensuring clarity in her marital eligibility.

en.hubeali: Ibn Mahboub, from Sa’dan Bin Muslim, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The man happens to have a concubine of his with him, and she had given birth from him, and her child had died. Then he emancipated her’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is not Permissible for her that he marries until she fulfills her waiting period of three months’.
